A fairly dry pattern is now in place across the Marianas, with only 
a few showers seen across the region. This dry pattern looks to 
continue through the end of the week. By Friday night, inflow into
Invest 91W looks to remain mostly outside of the area, however, it is
expected to bring an increased potential for thunderstorms to the
Marianas. Then, during the last half of the weekend, convection 
associated with Invest 90W looks to move into the region, increasing
POPs (Probability of Precipitation) into the 30 percent range across
the Marianas. A drier pattern is expected to return by the middle of
next week.

Marine...
Moderate to fresh winds will prevail across the Marianas for the 
next couple of days, with strong gusts over Tinian and Saipan 
waters. Winds are expected subside further, becoming gentle to 
moderate for the weekend. Large west swell will gradually subside
through Thursday, with the highest combined seas found over Tinian
and Saipan waters. The west swell will combine with wind waves and a
small southeast swell to maintain 10 foot seas across western waters
of both Tinian and Saipan through Thursday afternoon. For Guam and
Rota, seas will hover at around 9 feet through Thursday.

Tropical Systems...
A weak disturbance, Invest 90W, is centered northwest of Kwajalein 
near 12.1N 164.8E, moving slowly west-northwest. The Low-Level 
Circulation Center (LLCC) remains relatively cloud free, with the 
associated convection seen to the west of the center, along a band 
of convergence south of a col region. Invest 90W is expected to 
continue to move slowly west-northwest over the coming days with 
little change in intensity. Convection, however, may increase closer
to the center of 90W.

A more organized disturbance, Invest 91W, is centered west-northwest
of Maug Island near 21.8N 141.9E. Invest 91W has been upgraded to
high and is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert by
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), which means that tropical 
cyclone development is expected within the next 24 hours. Latest 
satellite data and surface analysis show a more organized cloud 
covered LLCC. Other factors remain favorable for TC development as 
well, with low vertical wind shear, good upper-level outflow and 
warm sea surface temperatures. The latest ASCAT analysis shows 25 to
30 knot winds to the south of 91W. Although Invest 91W is not 
expected to have a direct impact on the Marianas, increasing 
convection south of the monsoon trough and 91W could move into the 
Marianas, especially Tinian and Saipan northward, over the weekend. 
Invest 91W will continue to be monitored closely, and advisories will
be issued as needed.

For more information on Invest 91W, please see bulletins issued by 
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO header ABPW10 
PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A fairly dry pattern continues for Majuro with only isolated showers
in the area. Precipitable water remains high enough for showers to
become scattered tomorrow through Friday before a surge of moisture
from the south moves north from the Equator. This will likely stall 
south of Majuro and keep showers scattered, though the more unstable 
airmass will allow for isolated thunderstorms. Winds look to remain 
very light the entire forecast period.

For Pohnpei and Kosrae, a wetter pattern is moving in due to the
proximity of Invest 90W with high end scattered showers already
visible over Kosrae. Showers are forecasted to become numerous by the
weekend for both islands as 90W becomes more organized and the surge
of moisture from the Equator looks to move right over the islands.
This will also cause the light to moderate winds to shift from the 
northwest to the southwest by Friday night.

Strong southeast trades and a circulation south of the equator 
continue to generate south to southeast swell into eastern 
Micronesia. As the circulation meanders towards the Solomon Islands,
swell turns more southwest late week and over the weekend. For now, 
hazardous surf up to 8 feet is expected along south facing reefs of 
Kosrae through early Thursday morning, with another boost in surf 
heights likely to begin Saturday or Saturday night. A High Surf 
Advisory remains in effect along south facing reefs of Kosrae through
at least early Thursday morning.

Western Micronesia...
The pattern remains fairly quiet across western Micronesia, well 
south of the monsoon trough and associated disturbances. Mostly
cloudy skies developed over Yap and Palau this afternoon as swaths of
upper-level clouds swept overhead, debris from deep convection far to
the north. Meanwhile, mostly cloudy skies prevail across Chuuk,
associated with patchy showers in the area, which models are 
trending downward for tonight. Isolated showers are expected to then
